language-level.A1: Beginner — understands and uses very basic everyday expressions and phrases. Can introduce themselves and ask simple questions.
language-level.A2: Elementary — can communicate in simple and routine tasks, describe basic aspects of their life and environment.
language-level.B1: Intermediate — can understand main points of clear standard input on familiar matters like work or school.
language-level.B2: Upper intermediate — can interact with fluency and spontaneity with native speakers on general topics.
language-level.C1: Advanced — can express ideas fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions.
language-level.C2: Proficient — can understand virtually everything heard or read, summarize information, and express themselves precisely.
language-level.native: Native or bilingual — speaks the language as a mother tongue or with complete proficiency.

experience.Experts: Top-level professionals with 10+ years of experience. Provide strategic direction and solve complex problems.
experience.Seniors: Highly experienced professionals (5–10 years). Can lead projects and mentor others with autonomy.
experience.Confirmed: Mid-level professionals (3–5 years). Work independently and handle moderately complex tasks.
experience.Medium: Intermediate-level professionals with developing expertise (around 2–3 years of experience).
experience.Juniors: Entry-level professionals (0–2 years). Require guidance and supervision while learning core skills.

tool-expertise.basic: Has minimal familiarity with the tool — can perform only very simple operations with assistance.
tool-expertise.limited: Knows some basic functionalities but lacks confidence with advanced or complex tasks.
tool-expertise.intermediate: Comfortably uses common features and solves routine problems without supervision.
tool-expertise.advanced: Deeply understands tool features and can optimize workflows, scripts, or configurations.
tool-expertise.expert: Absolute mastery — capable of designing, optimizing, and troubleshooting complex tool usage scenarios.
